title: Color and tonal adjustment workflow for Sierra lupins (Part 5, 2023)

locations.name: Sierra (probable Sierra Nevada)
locations.basis: Filename includes 'Sierra' and transcript references mountainous terrain; explicit location not stated in transcript.

summary: The video presents a landscape-editing workflow aimed at balancing a warm foreground with a cool, blue-toned sky and purple lupins. It covers expanding dynamic range and lowering exposure, isolating processing by region (mountains, sky, flowers), gentle luminosity/midtone dodging for the flowers, then global color grading in Camera Raw followed by targeted color refinements in Photoshop via Selective Color to enhance magenta lupins and suppress distracting warm hues.

sections.title: Scene framing and color priorities
concepts: dual-color zones (golden/red sky vs purple/blue flower fields)
intent to maximize detail in both areas

sections.description: Introduces the scene with contrasting color zones and notes that blue in the sky and color in the flowers should be preserved and enhanced. Mentions the impact of white balance on color and references the wide-angle lens characteristic (12mm) that compresses mountains.

sections.title: Dynamic range and exposure management
sections.description: Demonstrates expanding the shot's dynamic range and then reducing overall exposure so highlights can be managed from the outset.

sections.title: Zone-based editing plan
concepts: separate processing by zones (mountains, sky, flowers)
avoid editing mountains and sky initially
focus adjustments on the flower region
sections.description: Outlines a workflow where processing is zoned, preserving the mountains and sky while enhancing the flowers.

sections.title: Luminosity adjustments and color grading workflow

Selective Color refinements to magenta in lupins
sections.description: Details a sequence of luminosity work (dodging) followed by color grading: increasing overall saturation with a subtle temperature shift, then targeted Selective Color tweaks to improve magenta tones in lupins and suppress undesirable warm hues.
